analysis: Fixed vs Random Model Sensitivity Analysis for G-theory
description: When model is treated as FIXED (not generalizing beyond these 8 models), sigma2(model:item)/n_model is removed from relative error variance delta, because model-specific item difficulty differences are systematic (known), not random error.

summary.conclusion: Treating models as fixed inflates G coefficients by 0.077-0.113 (mean +0.093) across all 5 benchmarks. The model:item interaction is the largest error component (14.6%-36.0% of total variance), so its inclusion in delta is consequential. Under the fixed-model assumption, all G values exceed 0.95, obscuring the substantial model-dependent item difficulty variation that real-world benchmark users face when selecting models. The random-model treatment is more conservative and appropriate when findings should generalize to models beyond the specific 8 tested.
